key_headlines.title: AI Boom Overshadows Middle East War Impact, WTO Doubles Trade Growth Forecast
key_headlines.summary: The World Trade Organization has more than doubled its forecast for global merchandise trade growth this year, as AI investment momentum significantly offsets energy and logistics disruptions from the Middle East conflict.

key_headlines.title: Semiconductor Material Shortage Intensifies as Prices Surge 30% on AI Chip Demand
key_headlines.summary: AI semiconductor demand explosion is driving widespread supply shortages across the entire semiconductor ecosystem, with substrate glass material prices rising 30% in Q3 alone despite Japanese supplier Nitto Denko's simultaneous capacity expansions.

key_headlines.title: US Oil Prices Surge 4% Despite Trump Delaying Iran Military Action
key_headlines.summary: Oil prices jumped 4% as market uncertainty persists over potential military operations against Iran, compounded by tanker attacks and production disruptions ahead of US midterm elections.

key_headlines.title: US Federal Fiscal Deficit Approaches $2 Trillion, Highest Since 2021
key_headlines.summary: The United States faces an unsustainable fiscal situation with a nearly $2 trillion budget deficit despite economic expansion and low unemployment, raising concerns about long-term fiscal health.

key_headlines.title: OpenAI Annual Revenue Revised Down to $50 Billion, 29% Below Previous Estimate
key_headlines.summary: OpenAI's actual annualized revenue is approximately $50 billion as of September, significantly lower than the previously reported $70 billion, reigniting concerns about AI sector valuation bubbles.

sections.Hot Economy News: The global economy is experiencing sharp divergence as AI investment booms overcome geopolitical disruptions. The WTO has more than doubled its world merchandise trade growth forecast for this year, reflecting strong AI-driven demand. However, the semiconductor supply chain is showing critical stress, with material shortages driving prices up 30% in Q3 alone. Oil markets remain volatile despite Trump's decision to postpone Iran military action, with prices surging 4% on continued uncertainties. Cybersecurity concerns have also emerged, with over 650 hacking attempts against South Korea's national finance system in the first seven months of 2026.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The United States faces a severe fiscal crisis with the federal deficit approaching $2 trillion in 2026, the highest level since 2021. Despite economic expansion and low unemployment, massive budget deficits continue to accumulate, raising serious concerns about fiscal sustainability. Rising interest rates on US government debt are compounding the problem, with Treasury Secretary and Federal Reserve officials struggling to contain costs. Trump administration's tariff policies have paradoxically reduced customs revenue while simultaneously driving up inflation and consumer prices. The combination of expansionary fiscal policy and monetary tightening is creating significant macroeconomic imbalances.
sections.Financial Markets: US Treasury yields have exceeded 5%, with some analysts warning of potential 6% levels, dramatically raising borrowing costs across the economy. Despite elevated rates, both equity and bond markets are attracting significant investment as S&P 500 large-cap stocks benefit from earnings expectations and bonds offer improved yield returns. South Korea's KOSPI index remains volatile amid global rate uncertainties and geopolitical tensions, though some ETF investors have achieved double-digit returns through selective strategies. Market sentiment is increasingly cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve's late-October rate decision and November midterm elections. The Kosdaq has outperformed the KOSPI, though expectations for recovery remain tempered by high interest rates.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's battery makers are posting strong Q3 results as global electric vehicle markets recover, with LG Energy Solution achieving record quarterly revenue and 26% operating profit growth. Hyundai Motor has surpassed 500,000 cumulative EV sales in Europe over the past decade, with Hyundai-Kia combined sales reaching 1.096 million units. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won reaffirmed commitment to Honam semiconductor cluster development, planning operations at approximately two-thirds the scale of the Yongin facility. The semiconductor industry continues to face supply chain pressures despite significant capital investments, requiring careful management of both production and material sourcing.
sections.Real Estate: South Korea's housing market faces multiple headwinds despite discussions of price stabilization, with five key variables set to influence property values. Seoul apartment prices remain elevated, with average 59-square-meter units priced at 1.59 billion won as of August, straining affordability amid maximum mortgage loan caps of 600 million won for regulated areas. Higher interest rates continue to suppress demand, with some prospective buyers exhausting savings to participate in apartment lotteries. Next week's apartment supply includes 1,829 units across the country, concentrated in Gyeonggi province areas like Hwaseong and Yangpyeong, reflecting ongoing housing development despite market uncertainties.
sections.International Economy: Global economic policy uncertainty is intensifying as the US Federal Reserve signals potential further rate increases through year-end, creating challenges for international markets. Federal Reserve officials remain divided on the pace of tightening, with some advocating for continued increases while others urge caution given economic impacts. Trump's tariff policies are producing negative consequences, with research showing consumer goods prices have risen 2.9 percentage points higher than they would have without tariffs. Rising US Treasury yields are generating spillover effects globally, affecting borrowing costs and currency dynamics worldwide. Geopolitical tensions, particularly regarding Ukraine and Iran, are adding additional uncertainty to energy prices and supply chains.
sections.AI & Economy: OpenAI's annual revenue has been revised downward to approximately $50 billion, representing a significant 29% reduction from the previously reported $70 billion figure based on miscalculations by investors. This discrepancy has reignited concerns about AI sector valuation bubbles and whether market expectations align with actual business fundamentals. Other AI startups are emerging rapidly, with some newly-founded companies achieving significant milestones; one 7-month-old startup with just 5 employees has surpassed Google's TensorFlow Marketplace and raised 4 billion won in initial funding. The AI market continues to expand, but with growing scrutiny of revenue claims and business models as companies compete for investor capital. Corporate AI adoption focuses increasingly on data-driven decision-making and productivity improvements rather than simple automation.
sections.Others: South Korea's National Tax Service has established new whistle-blower incentive structures for reporting tax evaders' hidden assets, though average compensation per case decreased compared to the previous year. The Finance Ministry has been largely unresponsive to National Tax Service legislative reform requests, rejecting approximately 80% of recommendations over the past three years. Global discussions are emerging regarding AI ethics and user conduct, with Anthropic implementing policies to sanction users engaging in persistent abuse toward AI chatbots. Geopolitical developments continue affecting economic policy, with the US requesting Ukraine suspend attacks on Russian refining facilities due to concerns about domestic fuel price impacts. Securities industry performance in Q3 has been disappointing following strong first-half results, with rising interest rates pressuring bond portfolio returns and real estate financing growth.
